Mixing averages E linearly but Δ only subadditively, and when two systems' influences are opposite, Δ of the mixture is zero while s_odd keeps its value: two systems at Δ_C = 0 pool to Δ_C = 0.6 (scratch/studies/lead-182/test_cbd.py). Without signalling the opposite holds, since the contextual fraction is convex under mixing ([THEORY-165](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-165.md)). So averaging over a counterbalanced factor, such as which character is named first, can manufacture contextuality, and [CASE-329](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-329.md) analyses each cell apart. The signalling term of the CbD criterion is a sum of absolute differences, and its plug-in estimate folds the sampling noise upward: at zero true signalling by about 4·√(2/π)·√(2/n), 0.23 at 400 respondents a context. The same bias makes an absence verdict anti-conservative: 84% false absence on the boundary. A Bonferroni bound crediting only guaranteed signalling is valid. [CLAIM-105](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-105.md)'s defeat condition asks for "a signalling estimator with bias correction"; this says what the bias costs and which way it cuts. | [CLAIM-937](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-937.md) | Signalling: valid tests, no unbiased estimator | Derived for [LEAD-072](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-072.md) on 2026-11-22 and checked by exact enumeration and simulation ([CASE-359](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-359.md)). Δ, a sum of absolute differences of binomial means, is not a polynomial in the probabilities, so no estimator is unbiased for it, whatever the counts; bias can be reduced, not removed. The squared difference is unbiasedly estimable, and its root halves the plug-in's bias where signalling is small, at a cost where it is large. What can be stated is an error: simultaneous Clopper-Pearson intervals for every marginal give an interval for Δ valid at any count, and exact per-content tests, combined by Bonferroni, give a test of the null that no content signals. Neither can say anything from one or two occurrences a context. This answers the estimator half of [CLAIM-235](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-235.md)'s request; the data half waits on counts [LIT-851](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-851.md) does not print. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
